title: scenarios: decide and write down whether a lint finding the author acknowledged with a reason counts against the build score
body:
epic:#34659#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnXJdSZifpEN5i7aU

Filing gate: ④ a child of the cross-lane parent #34659 (the 「MCP 二期与问数」 epic), filed on the maintainer's word in this session's chat, 2026-11-17, verbatim: 「立卡」, answering this session's list of four gaps nobody had carded. The gap was reported by the dispatching seat `repo:objectstack#3` on #34659 (comment 6961500641); the filer did not re-read the code behind it.

## Why

The scorecard charges a finding against a build even when the author acknowledged it and gave a reason. Whether that is intended is written nowhere, so two readers of the same score mean different things by it, and a build that handled a finding correctly scores like one that ignored it.

## Evidence

- Per the report (area o3-J's reading on #34895, 6961464499): `packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/orchestrate.ts` near line 753 counts an acknowledged finding.

## Scope

- The scorer's owner decides one of: it counts as today; it counts in a separate row; it does not count. This session's recommendation is a separate row: the build score then reads "nothing unhandled", and the acknowledged ones stay visible.
- The choice is written where the scorecard is described (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), and a round that changes it names the scorer sha, since scores before and after are not comparable.

## Done when

- The README states the rule and the runner follows it.

## Relations

- Parent: #34659. Related: #34895. Owner: the scenario scorer (`domain:devx`).
